this_week.title: The parable of the talents, audited.
this_week.verse: To whom much is given, much will be required.
this_week.summary: The servant who buried his talent didn't lose money. He just refused to put it to work. That's a perfectly acceptable financial control — and a perfectly terrible career move. This week we audit what we've been entrusted with, and what it costs to bury it.

stewardship_audit.hint: List the skills, relationships, data access, and responsibilities that landed in your lap this week — earned or not.
Name one output — a report, a query, a conversation — that used what you were given. Be specific. No filler.
Name one thing you knew how to do — but didn't. One insight you had — but didn't surface. This is where the audit gets honest.

stewardship_audit.q: What does the next week require?
stewardship_audit.hint: One commitment. Not a goal. A commitment. Something you'll have done by Friday that uses what you've been given.

stories.title: The Woman Who Killed a General With a Tent Peg
stories.summary: One of the greatest military victories in biblical history — won not by a soldier, a king, or a prophet. Jael wasn't on anybody's radar. She acted with the tools she had, right where she was. And history changed.

stories.title: The Man Swallowed by Something Worse Than a Whale
stories.summary: Everybody knows Jonah and the whale. But the real story is what happened after — a heart full of hatred disguised as religion, furious that God showed mercy to people Jonah had already written off.

stories.title: The King Who Went Insane and Ate Grass
stories.summary: The most powerful man on earth — crawling in a field, eating grass like an animal, for seven years. The moment he looked up and acknowledged something greater than himself, everything was restored.

stories.title: The Prophet Who Was Fed by Ravens
stories.summary: God told His boldest prophet to hide — and sent birds to feed him twice a day. The brook dried up. But it wasn't abandonment. It was redirection. The hidden season was never wasted.

stories.title: The Two Bears and the Mocking Children
stories.summary: Youths mocked the prophet — "baldhead." Two bears came out of the woods. One of the most uncomfortable passages in Scripture, and a clear warning: God's authority is not a joke.

stories.title: The Man Who Killed 600 With an Ox Goad
stories.summary: His entire story is one verse. No sword — a farming tool. Six hundred Philistine soldiers. Shamgar didn't wait for better equipment or more favorable circumstances. He used what was in his hand.

stories.title: The Witch of Endor and the Dead Prophet
stories.summary: A desperate king, a forbidden medium, and a dead prophet summoned from the grave. What Samuel's voice told Saul was not comfort — it was a final accounting of a kingdom mishandled one small disobedience at a time.

stories.title: The Man Who Touched the Ark and Died Instantly
stories.summary: He was just trying to help — the ark was falling. But good intentions don't override God's instructions. How you carry a sacred thing matters as much as whether you carry it at all.

stories.title: The Angel Who Killed 185,000 Soldiers Overnight
stories.summary: One night. One angel. An entire Assyrian army dead by morning — because Hezekiah took the enemy's threatening letter to the temple and spread it out before God instead of fighting alone.

stories.title: The Man Who Stopped the Sun
stories.summary: Joshua didn't ask for a general blessing. He commanded the sun to stand still — out loud, in front of everyone. The God who stopped the sun for Joshua is the same God who hears your prayer today.

stories.title: The Midwives Who Defied a Pharaoh and Saved a Nation
stories.summary: Before Moses ever floated in a basket, two Hebrew midwives were ordered to kill every newborn boy. They said no. A nation survived because Shiphrah and Puah feared God more than they feared the most powerful man alive.

stories.title: The Mother Who Let Her Son Go
stories.summary: Hannah prayed so hard the priest thought she was drunk. God heard the prayer no one could even see. Then she received the miracle she prayed for — and gave him back to God. What she surrendered changed history.

stories.title: The Little Servant Girl Who Saved a General
stories.summary: She had no name, no power, and every reason to stay silent. Four sentences from a kidnapped child set the greatest healing miracle of Elisha's ministry in motion. You don't need a platform to change a life.

stories.title: The Woman Who Wouldn't Stop Until She Got Justice
stories.summary: Jesus told this parable specifically to address the feeling that prayers are going unanswered. The widow's persistence wasn't annoying to Jesus — it was the example He pointed to. Don't stop asking.

stories.title: Five Sisters Who Changed the Law
stories.summary: They walked to the most sacred, public space in Israel and stated their case before Moses and the entire assembly. God ruled in their favor — and changed the law for every daughter who came after them.

stories.title: The Grandmother Who Shaped a Nation's Faith
stories.summary: Paul credited Timothy's extraordinary faith not to a great teacher or a dramatic conversion — but to a grandmother named Lois. What she modeled in ordinary moments changed the ancient world.

stories.title: The Child Who Heard God's Voice at Night
stories.summary: A boy sleeping in the temple, called by name three times in the dark. He ran to Eli each time before anyone understood what was happening. God calls young people — and He calls them by name.

stories.title: The Mother Who Split a Baby to Save It
stories.summary: Two mothers. One living baby. A king's impossible judgment. The real mother would rather lose her child to a stranger than see him die — and that willingness to let go proved her love.

stories.title: The Girl Who Danced a Man to His Death
stories.summary: A birthday party. A dance. A king's foolish oath. The head of John the Baptist on a platter — because a girl raised in her mother's hatred became an instrument of it. The bitterness we carry flows into those we raise.

stories.title: The Woman Who Anointed Jesus When No One Else Understood
stories.summary: She broke a jar worth a year's wages over Jesus. The room called it waste. Jesus called it beautiful — and said it would be told wherever the gospel is preached. She understood what the disciples had missed.

stories.title: The Good Samaritan — The Story That Redefined "Neighbor"
stories.summary: The priest passed. The Levite passed. Jesus' answer to "who is my neighbor?" destroyed the idea that religion qualifies you to decide who deserves your compassion. Your neighbor is whoever the road puts in front of you.

stories.title: Jesus Feeds Five Thousand With a Boy's Lunch
stories.summary: A boy offered his whole lunch to a stranger. He had no idea it would feed twenty thousand people. You don't need to have enough to make a difference — just bring what you have to the right hands.

stories.title: Jesus and the Man Nobody Would Touch
stories.summary: He hadn't been touched by another human being in years. Jesus reached out and touched him — before healing him, before saying a word. The touch was the first miracle. Then came the rest.

stories.title: The Rich Man Who Walked Away Sad
stories.summary: He kept all the commandments, ran to Jesus, and genuinely wanted eternal life. Mark says Jesus looked at him and loved him — then asked for the one thing he couldn't give. The greatest obstacle is rarely the obvious sin.

stories.title: The Sheep, the Coin, and the Son — Three Parables About the Lost
stories.summary: Three things lost. Three parties when found. The father who ran — undignified, watching the road — is the picture Jesus drew of God. Heaven throws a party over one person coming home.

stories.title: Jesus at the Well — The Woman the World Gave Up On
stories.summary: She came to the well alone at noon, carrying a history everyone knew. Jesus already knew it too — and waited there anyway. The woman the town had rejected became the town's evangelist.

stories.title: Zacchaeus — The Man Who Climbed a Tree to See Jesus
stories.summary: A wealthy, despised tax collector abandoned his dignity to climb a sycamore just to see Jesus. Jesus stopped, looked up, and called him by name. By dinner's end, Zacchaeus committed half his wealth to the poor.

stories.title: The Widow's Offering — When Two Coins Outweigh a Fortune
stories.summary: The wealthy gave large, visible amounts. A poor widow dropped in two copper coins. Jesus called His disciples over and said she gave more than all of them. God doesn't measure giving by amount — He measures by proportion and love.

stories.title: Jesus Heals on the Sabbath — When Rules Replaced Compassion
stories.summary: He had been waiting by the pool for 38 years. Jesus asked the one uncomfortable question: "Do you want to get well?" Then He healed him — and the religious leaders' response was outrage, not rejoicing.

stories.title: The Sheep and the Goats — How Jesus Says He'll Judge the World
stories.summary: Jesus described Judgment Day — and the criteria had almost nothing to do with what most people expect. It was about hungry people, strangers, the sick, and prisoners. How you treat the least is how you treat Him.

accounting.s: A debit increases an asset account.
accounting.why: Assets carry a normal debit balance — debits increase them.
Revenue carries a normal credit balance.

accounting.s: A debit increases a liability account.
accounting.why: Liabilities carry a credit balance — debits decrease them.

accounting.s: Accumulated depreciation is a contra-asset account.
accounting.why: It offsets the related asset with a credit balance.

accounting.s: Prepaid expenses are recorded as liabilities.
accounting.why: Prepaids are assets — future benefit already paid for.

accounting.s: Under accrual accounting, revenue is recognized when cash is received.
accounting.why: Revenue is recognized when earned, not when cash arrives.

accounting.s: Retained earnings normally carries a credit balance.
accounting.why: It's an equity account — normal credit balance.

accounting.s: The accounting equation is Assets = Liabilities + Equity.
A trial balance that balances proves the ledger has no errors.
accounting.why: Offsetting or omitted entries can still balance.
Dividends are a distribution of equity.

accounting.s: Unearned revenue is a liability until it is earned.
accounting.why: You owe the customer performance — that's a liability.

accounting.s: Expenses normally carry a credit balance.
accounting.why: Expenses carry a normal debit balance.

data.s: The median is more resistant to outliers than the mean.
data.why: Extreme values pull the mean, not the median.
Correlated variables can share a hidden common cause.

data.s: In SQL, WHERE filters rows before GROUP BY aggregates them.
data.why: WHERE runs pre-aggregation; HAVING runs after.

data.s: A LEFT JOIN returns only rows that match in both tables.
data.why: That's an INNER JOIN — LEFT keeps all left-side rows.

data.s: Standard deviation is the square root of variance.
data.why: By definition — same units as the data.

data.s: In SQL, HAVING filters aggregated results.
data.why: HAVING applies conditions after GROUP BY.

data.s: A p-value below 0.05 proves the null hypothesis is false.
data.why: It suggests evidence against it — never proof.

data.s: Normalization reduces data redundancy in relational databases.
A histogram shows the distribution of one numeric variable.
data.why: Bars represent frequency across value bins.

data.s: Overfitting means a model performs better on new data than training data.
data.why: It's the opposite — great on training, poor on new data.

data.s: In a boxplot, the box spans the interquartile range.
data.why: Q1 to Q3, with the median line inside.

data.s: COUNT(*) in SQL skips rows containing NULL values.
data.why: COUNT(*) counts every row; COUNT(col) skips NULLs.

clues: I welcomed a fleeing general into my tent.
I gave him milk when he asked for water.
My weapon was a tent peg.
I ran from an assignment to Nineveh.
I slept through a storm that terrified sailors.
A great fish gave me three days to reconsider.
I ruled the greatest empire of my day.
A dream about a chopped-down tree troubled me.
I ate grass until I acknowledged heaven rules.
I told a king there would be no rain.
I hid by a brook east of the Jordan.
Ravens brought me bread and meat.
My mother dedicated me before I was born.
I served under an old priest in the temple.
I ran to old Eli three times in the night before we realized Who was calling.
I wept and prayed until a priest thought I was drunk.
I promised my son to the Lord.
I brought him a little robe every year.
Two women brought me one living baby.
I called for a sword to settle it.
My verdict revealed the true mother.
I was taken captive from Israel.
I served the wife of an army commander.
I pointed my master toward the prophet who could heal his leprosy.
I collected taxes in Jericho.
I was too short to see over the crowd.
I climbed a sycamore tree — and dinner changed my life.
I came to draw water at noon, alone.
A stranger asked me for a drink.
He told me everything I ever did.

Until both are set per product, that product shows no buy button — the app will never take money it cannot fulfil. Flip this flag and bump version to go live; no app release needed.
